rows.what_the_ink_shows: The cokernel sentence ends with a heavily cancelled expression and a replacement above it (crops/56_scan005_L195_cokernel.png and crops/56_scan005_L195_generator.png). The replacement has a curved left arm, a closed right loop, and a long central descender, followed by a nu-shaped subscript. The open, forked lambda shapes elsewhere on the same page are different (crops/56_scan005_L195_lambda_comparison.png and crops/56_scan005_L195_lambda_prime_comparison.png). The later main-reader comparison with the explicit varphi_nu form in the supplied 56/026 diagram shows the same left arm, loop and descender (crops/56_scan026_L195_phi_comparison.png). This supports inserted varphi_nu, not lambda_nu. The crossed-out predecessor remains too worked to settle, so its existing deleted/doubt markup is preserved.
rows.note: The initial page-only reader could not identify the looped replacement and retained the doubtful lambda. The main reader initially preserved that doubt, then recognized the matching varphi form while reviewing the supplied 56/026 page. The final transcription corrects only the surviving replacement to inserted varphi_nu and preserves the uncertain cancelled predecessor. It does not substitute the editorial symbol l_a. L195 supplies the mathematical explanation that one ruling class generates the cokernel, whereas lambda_nu=l_a-l_b gives twice that class modulo the image and needs 2 invertible. This supplied explanation is recorded without an independent proof or an assertion that the manuscript explicitly labels varphi_nu as l_a on this page. The prior b disposition and both main-reader checks remain in the audit trail.
